description: The Onyx visual identity: the Onyx Dark and Onyx Light color themes and the getting-started walkthrough for local AI features.
walkthrough.title: Get Started with Onyx
walkthrough.description: Local models, an adaptive agent, and a control plane that shows you everything.
walkthrough.runtime.title: Connect a local runtime
walkthrough.runtime.description:
Onyx runs every AI feature against models on your own machine — no cloud, no telemetry.
[Show Local Runtimes](command:onyx.showLocalRuntimes)
walkthrough.auto.title: Chat with Auto routing
walkthrough.auto.description:
Ask the Onyx agent anything. The Auto model routes each request to the best local model for the job — and learns from how you use it.
[Open Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)
walkthrough.controlPlane.title: Open the Control Plane
walkthrough.controlPlane.description:
Watch every agent step live with the reason behind it, inspect exactly what the model was sent token by token, and see what it cost in compute — per model, for this session and all time.
[Open Onyx Control Plane](command:onyx.openControlPlane)
walkthrough.models.title: Pick models that fit your Mac
walkthrough.models.description:
The model library reads this machine's unified memory and tells you which models actually fit, at which quantization and context window — then installs them with one click.
[Manage Models](command:onyx.manageModels)
walkthrough.review.title: Commit and review locally
walkthrough.review.description:
Write commit messages from the staged diff, run an adversarial reviewer over your working tree, and fix or explain code without leaving the editor.
[Review My Changes](command:onyx.reviewChanges)
walkthrough.verification.title: Benchmark and verify
walkthrough.verification.description:
Benchmark your models to sharpen routing, and let Onyx run your project's checks after the agent edits code.
[Benchmark Local Models](command:onyx.benchmarkModels)
